transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

[Heading: Probably normal]
That 3 hours 39 minutes is actually the correct time for an Eco 40-60 cycle on modern machines. These programmes are designed to save energy by washing at lower temperatures for longer periods, which is why they take significantly longer than older 'standard' 40°C cycles that used higher heat and shorter times. It is not faulty, so you do not need to send it back. If the laundry comes out warm after that cycle, your new machine is heating perfectly fine; if it stays cold, then we would look into a heating fault.

The door glass is only barely lukewarm during the wash, and the water barely feels warm if I touch it. The clothes do come out clean though. Is that normal for a 40 wash, or does it mean the heating isn't working?

[Heading: Normal Eco programme operation]
This is normal. The Eco 40-60 cycle is designed to wash at a lower temperature (around 40°C) for a much longer time to save energy. Because the water isn't boiling hot and the machine spends hours tumbling in cooler water, the door glass and the water itself will only feel lukewarm or barely warm to the touch. You do not need to send it back; just allow the cycle to finish as programmed.
